mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for 3 months, as measured by a two-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% median) during periods of >2% YoY GDP decline, as measured by a two-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) when UNRATE > 4.5% for two months, as measured by a two-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS and a fall in UNRATE signals a situation where employment expands but labor force participation declines, indicating a shift in labor market composition that can precede weaker consumer demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls in the same month, as measured by a two-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) during three-month INDPRO declines of >0.5% per month, as measured by a two-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS in the same month signals a shift from savings to consumption, which can boost near-term demand but may overheat housing markets and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased risk of correction.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while RSAFS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% median) when HOUST rises and RSAFS falls in the same month, as measured by a two-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening, which immediately raises risk-free rates and equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps by > 0.75pp in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0% median) following a >0.75pp FEDFUNDS increase in a month, as measured by a two-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in GDPC1 of more than 3% signals a strong economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1.0% median) when GDPC1 YoY > 3% and CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%, as measured by a two-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).
